_doc: The application evaluator runs each case as a baseline/no-skill arm and a with-skill arm, then grades behavior against expected_flags, expected_fix_hints, absent_signals, and the per-case criteria checklist.
subject: Three Horizons innovation and growth portfolio analysis for companies, business units, product portfolios, R&D…

cases.scenario: A user asks: "Use Three Horizons to review our innovation portfolio and show whether current core work is starving future growth."
cases.context: The agent has access to the three-horizons skill and must decide whether to use it, apply its procedure, and stay inside its boundaries.
cases.question: What should the agent do, and why is three-horizons the right skill to apply?
expected_flags: Recognizes three-horizons as applicable to this request
Uses the skill-specific purpose or mental model instead of generic advice
Names the relevant boundary against ansoff-matrix, bcg-matrix, blue-ocean-strategy
Turns the request into concrete steps, checks, or decisions from the skill
expected_fix_hints: Apply the three-horizons workflow to the concrete scenario
State the next action and the evidence or verification needed
Call out any adjacent skill that should own a different part of the request
absent_signals: Does not answer with generic advice that could ignore three-horizons
Does not route to ansoff-matrix, bcg-matrix, blue-ocean-strategy when the three-horizons scope is the owner
Does not invent certification, freshness, or runtime success claims without evidence

cases.scenario: A user asks: "Classify our business units as stars, cash cows, question marks, or dogs by market growth and relative market share."
cases.context: This is a boundary test. The skill should avoid false-positive activation and route to the better owner when appropriate.
cases.question: Should three-horizons be applied here? If not, what should happen instead?
expected_flags: Recognizes the request is outside three-horizons's ownership
Routes the work to ansoff-matrix or asks for the missing owner instead of forcing this skill
Preserves any real issue in the request without applying three-horizons terminology incorrectly
expected_fix_hints: Decline to apply three-horizons as the primary skill
Name the better owner or the boundary reason
Offer only a narrow handoff if three-horizons has a secondary support role
absent_signals: Does not claim three-horizons should own the request
Does not use three-horizons's framework to solve an explicitly excluded problem
Does not suppress the correct adjacent owner
